subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should OpenClaw replace the released `getAcpSessionManager()` nominal class contract immediately, or stage the restricted facade through an additive and versioned transition?
rationale: Preserving the existing manager instance would undermine the intended isolation boundary once private recovery writers land, while replacing it now deliberately breaks a shipped third-party Plugin SDK contract; repository policy cannot choose that tradeoff automatically.

options.title: Stage an additive facade
options.body: Add a distinct facade getter, migrate internal and known plugin consumers, deprecate the class-returning getter, and delay private recovery writers until an approved removal boundary.

options.title: Approve the immediate break
options.body: Explicitly accept the v2026.7.1 compatibility break, require clear plugin upgrade guidance, and verify the new boundary in a compiled runtime before merge.

options.title: Pause the recovery stack
options.body: Keep the split series unmerged until a different private-state ownership design avoids changing the released manager identity contract.

recommendation.title: Stage an additive facade
recommendation.body: Add a distinct facade getter, migrate internal and known plugin consumers, deprecate the class-returning getter, and delay private recovery writers until an approved removal boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the foundational ACP implementation and is the strongest available owner for deciding its released Plugin SDK compatibility boundary.
